summary: Sonya S. Lee is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago and taught at Swarthmore College before holding posts at the University of Southern California and Stanford University.

Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, later holding a post at Dongguk University.
Soorakkulame Pemarathana specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his studies at the National University of Singapore, where Saranindranath Tagore served as his thesis supervisor.
Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held an academic post at Uppsala University and taught Sten Konow.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.
Soshuku Shibatani specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University, attested in 2015.

Sravana Borkataky-Varma works in religious studies and Indology. She held posts at the University of North Carolina Wilmington (circa 2017–2020), the University of Houston (circa 2020), and Harvard University (circa 2020–2021).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma works in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Visva-Bharati University, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD circa 1963–1966), he served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University, attested 2006–2012.

Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, sinology, history, and archaeology. She earned an MA from the University of Colorado Boulder and a PhD from Columbia University, where she held a post attested in 2013.

Stanislas Julien was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat at the Collège de France. He succeeded Abel-Rémusat in 1832, serving at the Collège de France as professor and administrator until 1873.
Stanley Abe specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held an academic post at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Insler was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Columbia College, Yale University, and the University of Tübingen, he held a faculty post at Yale University from circa 1964 to 2012.

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Ceylon, Cornell, and Harvard, he held posts at the University of Cambridge and Harvard University, serving as Professor of Anthropology from circa 1976 to 2001.

Stanley Weinstein was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology who studied at Harvard University. He was a professor at the University of London (circa 1962–1968) and later served as emeritus professor at Yale University.

Stanley Wolpert was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, he served as a distinguished professor emeritus of history at UCLA from circa 1959 to 2002.
Stefan Anacker was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from circa 1964 to 1970 under the supervision of Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who completed his dissertation at the University of Washington. He held posts at the University of Copenhagen, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and LMU Munich.

Stefan Larsson specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stockholm University in 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Berkeley, attested in 2012.
Stefan Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the Free University of Berlin from 1987 to 1995 and at Heidelberg University beginning in 1995.

Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She served as an assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen (circa 2013–2020) and held a post at SOAS University of London around 2020.
